Getting started with paperrepo

Source: vignettes/paperrepo.Rmd
paperrepo.Rmd

The paperrepo package creates a consistent, reproducible workspace for an empirical research paper. This vignette walks through the main workflow from project creation to manuscript rendering and handoff.

Create a project

Create a fresh directory for each paper. The default scaffold is deliberately small enough to understand at a glance, but includes all of the locations needed for a complete analysis.

~{r create-project, eval=FALSE} paperrepo::create_paper_project( path = “my-paper”, project_name = “My empirical paper” ) ~

If renv is not installed, the package writes a starting lockfile and explains how to initialize the environment. Once renv is available, run renv::snapshot() after adding analysis dependencies.

Follow the analysis sequence

The generated R directory is intentionally numbered:

  1. 01-import.R reads and documents raw inputs.
  2. 02-clean.R creates analysis-ready data.
  3. 03-analyze.R estimates models and writes machine-readable results.
  4. 04-export.R creates tables and figures used by the manuscript.

Run the sequence from the project root:

Rscript scripts/run-analysis.R

Keep exploratory work in sandbox/ until it is stable enough to promote into the numbered scripts. Keep non-R utilities in code/.

Write and render the manuscript

The manuscript source is paper.qmd. Its metadata declares HTML, Word, and PDF formats, and PDF output keeps the generated TeX. Render all formats together:

~{r render-all, eval=FALSE} paperrepo::render_paper(“my-paper”, formats = “all”) ~

Or render a subset:

~{r render-selected, eval=FALSE} paperrepo::render_paper(“my-paper”, formats = c(“pdf”, “docx”)) paperrepo::render_paper(“my-paper”, formats = “html”) ~

Rendered files go to output/manuscript/. A PDF render refreshes paper.tex at the project root, where it can be inspected and supplied to a journal.

Keep a decision trail

Use notes/active.md for current tasks and open questions. Archive completed or superseded decisions with a date:

~{r archive-note, eval=FALSE} paperrepo::archive_note( title = “Resolve missingness decision”, body = “Compare complete-case and weighted estimates.”, path = “my-paper” ) ~

The note is written to notes/archive/ and linked from notes/INDEX.md.

Validate a handoff

Before sharing the repository, check its structure and rerun the manuscript from a clean session:

~{r check-project, eval=FALSE} paperrepo::check_paper_project(“my-paper”) ~

The generated README also contains a reproducibility checklist covering data provenance, derived files, package snapshots, and journal submission.
